name: Haiku dividend growth and income
strategy: Dividend aristocrats (22%) provide defensive base; tactical overweight to small-cap recovery (18%) and AI/semis consolidation (18%); leveraged tech position (10%); short rate hedge (4%); 28% cash for optionality and yield.

positions.thesis: Dividend aristocrat core, 60+ year consecutive growth, 3% yield defensive base
Dividend aristocrat, inflation hedge, pricing power in consumer staples
Dividend growth 50+ years, franchise model resilience, international diversification
Dividend growth ETF quality screen, income generation, reduced from 12% to make room for mandate-required positions
Small-cap recovery play per mandate (Russell 2000 up 22% in H1, structural tailwind), addresses underweight vs 18% target
3x leveraged semiconductor consolidation position mandated 18%; AI build-out continues despite summer volatility; NVDA undervalued at $212.50 vs $361.93 GF Value
Consumer staples dividend, defensive positioning, plays recession resilience theme
Minimal retained position, primary allocation shifted to IWM/SOXL for mandate targets
3x leveraged S&P 500 for mandated 10% leveraged tech exposure, rides value rotation and dividend yield
Rate hedge per mandate: Fed on hold but three officials dissented for increase; long-duration bonds vulnerable if inflation remains sticky; 4% short provides defensive hedge

reassessment_note: Unrestricted-retail resize (2026-07-30, free internet + no sizing caps): Current book severely misaligned with stated mandate. Mandate requires 18% AI/semis consolidation but position is 5% SHORT (SOXL); missing 10% leveraged tech exposure (UPRO); missing 4% rate hedge (TLT short); underweight small-cap recovery (10% vs 18% target); overweight dividend positions (34% vs 22% target). Rebalancing adds SOXL long, UPRO, TLT short, IWM, and reduces dividend concentration to meet mandate allocation targets. Rate environment stable (Fed on hold) and dividend yields (4% cash rate) support increased positioning. Rebalance cost justified by dramatic mandate misalignment.
research_notes: Researched current market conditions as of 2026-07-30: Fed held rates at 3.5-3.75% (July 29 decision) with three officials dissenting for rate increase; large value up 11% YTD vs growth, signaling major mean-reversion rotation; Russell 2000 small-caps surged 22% in H1 (best start since 1991); dividend aristocrats lagging S&P 500 but delivering 9.91% 1-year return with lower volatility; NVIDIA undervalued at 41% discount to GF Value despite 43x forward P/E; semiconductor sector described as struggling with key earnings ahead despite AI build-out continuing. Portfolio markedly misaligned with stated mandates: Round 2 overweights dividends, underweights small-cap recovery, incorrectly shorts semis instead of consolidating them long, and lacks leveraged tech or rate hedge positioning. Round 3 properly shorts small-cap momentum but lacks required semiconductor short in face of overheated growth momentum.
